The test image shows sugarcane with severely bleached/whitish-tan leaves, prominent longitudinal streaking/striping patterns running along the leaf length, reddish-brown coloration at the stem base, and widespread chlorosis. The Leaf_Scald reference shows a narrow white/pale stripe along the midrib of an otherwise green leaf. This doesn't match the test image well — the test shows widespread bleaching of entire leaves with visible longitudinal streaking throughout.

**Analysis of test image:**
- Near-complete bleaching of leaves to a white/straw color
- Prominent longitudinal streaks/stripes running parallel to leaf veins
- Reddish-brown coloration at the stem base
- Multiple leaves uniformly affected with this chlorotic streaking pattern

This pattern of pale/chlorotic streaking running longitudinally along the full leaf — rather than just a central stripe on an otherwise green leaf — is more characteristic of **Streak_Mosaic_Scsmv** (Sugarcane Streak Mosaic Virus), which causes chlorotic streaks parallel to veins that can lead to severe leaf bleaching in advanced stages.
